A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal algorithm for evaluating a window join over two streams depends on both the relative speed and the relative size of the two streams, and that it is important to allocate resources (both CPU and memory) properly to achieve the best possible performance.

we can maximize resource utilization and/or the number of join tuples produced by carefully allocating resources across the two inputs and by using asymmetric combinations of join algorithm implementations.
the best strategy is to allocate resources to each of the streams according to the rate of the streams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal algorithm for a given window join depends not only on the characteristics of the input streams but also on the characteristics of system resources.
the optimal join algorithm for a given scenario is highly dependent on the characteristics of the input streams and system resources.

, in many cases, the optimal strategy for evaluating window joins over unbounded streams can be determined without knowing the actual characteristics of the input streams, but rather by knowing only the expected characteristics of the input.
